title: Landslide Safety
description: Landslides occur when masses of rock, earth, or debris move down a slope. Recognizing warning signs and knowing how to respond can protect lives in hilly and mountainous areas.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: A landslide is the movement of rock, earth, or debris down a sloped section of land. Landslides are caused by gravity acting on weakened materials that make up a sloping area of land. They can be triggered by heavy rainfall, earthquakes, volcanic activity, changes in slope stability, or human activities such as construction and mining. Landslides can occur suddenly with little warning and cause significant damage to buildings, roads, and infrastructure. India's hilly regions, particularly in the Himalayas and Western Ghats, are prone to landslides.

sections.heading: Warning Signs
sections.content: Learn to recognize landslide warning signs such as cracks appearing in the ground or on foundations of buildings. Tilting of trees, poles, or fences can indicate slope movement. Changes in water flow patterns, such as water emerging from new locations or blocked drainage, may indicate landslide activity. Unusual sounds such as trees cracking or boulders knocking together can signal moving debris. Bulging ground at the base of a slope and small rockfalls are also warning signs. If you notice these signs, evacuate immediately.

sections.heading: Before a Landslide
sections.content: If you live in a landslide-prone area, identify escape routes and safe areas away from the slope. Avoid building on steep slopes or close to mountain edges. Plant ground cover on slopes to stabilize the soil. Properly divert drainage away from slopes. Do not build near the base of steep hills or at the top of cliffs. Create an emergency kit with food, water, medications, flashlight, battery-powered radio, first aid supplies, and important documents. Monitor weather forecasts during heavy rainfall seasons. Know how to contact local emergency services.

sections.heading: During a Landslide
sections.content: If you are inside a building and suspect a landslide is imminent, evacuate immediately. Move to the highest level of the building if you cannot evacuate outdoors. Do not use elevators during evacuation. If you are outdoors, move away from the path of the landslide as quickly as possible. Move perpendicular to the direction of the landslide flow. Do not try to outrun a landslide—move sideways to escape its path. If you are in a vehicle, do not attempt to drive through a landslide area. Abandon the vehicle and move to safety on foot if possible.

sections.heading: After a Landslide
sections.content: Stay away from the landslide area until authorities declare it safe. Additional landslides can occur in the same area. Check for injuries and provide first aid if needed. Listen to radio or TV for emergency information and instructions. Report damaged utility lines to authorities. Do not drink tap water until officials confirm it is safe. Be cautious of damaged roads and bridges. Document damage with photographs for insurance purposes. Help neighbors if you can do so safely. Be prepared for possible road closures and transportation disruptions.

sections.heading: Safety Precautions
sections.content: Never ignore landslide warning signs or evacuation orders. Avoid areas with visible slope movement or recent landslide activity. Do not build or park vehicles near steep slopes or cliffs. Stay alert during and after heavy rainfall, which is a common landslide trigger. Do not attempt to cross areas where a landslide has occurred until cleared by authorities. Be especially cautious in areas where vegetation has been removed by fire or logging. Follow all instructions from emergency responders and local authorities. If you must evacuate, do not return until officials declare it safe.
